_note: Ground truth for comparing keyframing methods (scripts/keyframe_bench.py). Per video, 'required' windows [t0, t1] in seconds: the paper holds a new state after a fold or flip, from the moment the fold is finished until the next manipulation starts. A method hits a state when it picks a frame inside its window. 'optional' windows are frames that are fine to pick but not required (rotation, unfold back to a creased sheet, colouring, gluing eyes, in-hand 3D shaping): the first pick there is neutral. An optional window with a third number re-shows that required state; a pick there hits the state if nothing else did, otherwise it is a duplicate. Anything outside all windows (title cards, mid-fold frames, end cards, stems) is an extra. Labelled from 1 fps contact sheets (2 fps where the video is fast), so edges are +-0.5 s.
